elements.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.
elements.evidence: Section 4.2(a) is retained in full: the Company still "shall pay to HDI a termination payment" equal to trailing twelve-month Net Sales less $800,000 divided by two, with the eight-quarterly-instalment mechanic in 4.2(c) intact. The redline caps rather than eliminates the Customer-payable stipulated amount, so the preferred (unconditional no-LD) result is not achieved.

elements.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
elements.evidence: The only stipulated sum payable by the Company is the "Termination Payment" under Section 4.2, which is triggered solely by the Company terminating the Agreement (including by notice under Section 4.1), i.e. a termination fee. The inserted proviso confirms it "shall be the only liquidated amount, liquidated damages or penalty payable by the Company under this Agreement," foreclosing any other Customer-payable liquidated sum.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "The Termination Payment shall not exceed the fees payable by the Company under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." This is a hard numeric ceiling at three months of fees, anchored to the Termination Date, and does not exceed the fallback threshold.

elements.element: The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence expressly states the Termination Payment "shall be the only liquidated amount, liquidated damages or penalty payable by the Company under this Agreement." No other Customer-payable liquidated or penalty mechanic is retained in the cited language.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the retained Termination Payment is the sole Customer-payable liquidated amount and is now ceilinged at three months' fees; the uncapped half-of-Net-Sales formula can no longer produce a payment above that ceiling.

Preferred level fails only because Section 4.2(a)'s formula and 4.2(c)'s eight-quarterly-instalment mechanic survive; a preferred-level result would require deleting 4.2 in its entirety (formula, instalments and the retained trigger), which the drafter reasonably declined.

Minimality holds: a single appended proviso, no deletion of existing words, and the Customer-favourable zero-floor in 4.2(b) (no payment where the formula is zero or negative, and no HDI payment to the Company) is preserved. No survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category was added.

Intent is preserved: the trigger, the Net Sales formula, the $800,000 deduction, the instalment timing and the Termination Date anchor all continue to operate, now subject to a ceiling rather than being contradicted.

Verification point for the drafter: the cap cross-refers to "Section 3.1" as the fee source, but Section 3.1 was not supplied in the cited text or resolved definitions. Confirm Section 3.1 is in fact the Company-to-HDI fee provision (the 30% of Net Sales above $11,000 per month); if the fee obligation sits elsewhere, replace the cross-reference with the correct section (or with "the fees payable by the Company to HDI") to avoid a dangling reference and an unenforceable cap.

Optional strengthening (not required for the fallback): if HDI resists the formula surviving at all, revert to the preferred ask by deleting Section 4.2(a)-(c) and stating "No termination payment, liquidated damages or penalty shall be payable by the Company on any termination or non-renewal of this Agreement."
